comparator.name: Biomedische wetenschappen
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations require a 135 EC major and 45 EC of profiling space. The major comprises 75 EC of compulsory courses and 60 EC of major choices, including a required research project. This outline uses the standard 15 EC project and keeps the elective space open. At least five courses must come from the ten-course major list, including Molecular Cell Biology.

core: Molecular, cellular, biochemical and genetic mechanisms of human health and disease
Human anatomy, physiology, tissues and organ-system function
Disease mechanisms, cancer, infection and immunity
Biomedical research, laboratory methods, statistics, bioinformatics and data
Translation from biomedical research to diagnosis, treatment and clinical medicine
Ethical, societal and communication dimensions of biomedical impact
adjacent: Neuroscience, cognition and behaviour as human biomedical systems
Population health, prevention and environmental health risk
Computational and quantitative analysis of biomedical evidence
questions: How do molecular, cellular and genetic processes cause disease?
How are biomedical discoveries translated into diagnosis and treatment?
How can cancer, infection and other major health problems be understood and prevented?

candidates.label: Molecular genetics, cancer and biomedical data
Human physiology, disease and mental health

alternatives.label: Human biology, disease and biomedical research
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule follows the comparator's molecules-to-organism biomedical core, disease mechanisms, laboratory and quantitative research, translation and societal impact.
alternatives.concept: Study how cells, genes and organs function in health and disease. Combine laboratory work and statistics with anatomy, infection, pharmacology and epidemiology to investigate mechanisms of disease and evidence for prevention.
progression: The life-science gateway precedes dependent biomedical study. Molecular Cell Biology and Life Science Laboratory precede pathology and disease. Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics.

alternatives.label: Molecular genetics, cancer and biomedical data
alternatives.labelReason: Direct interests in molecular and cellular illness and genetics support a computationally stronger biomedical route centred on pathology, cancer-relevant disease mechanisms and research data.
alternatives.concept: Study genetic variation, cellular mechanisms and disease, including cancer. Combine laboratory work with programming, data management, statistics, machine learning and image analysis to explore how computational methods can be used in biomedical research.
progression: Programming and mathematics precede advanced algorithms and deep learning. Introductory data handling precedes machine learning and deep learning. Molecular Cell Biology and Life Science Laboratory precede pathology.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses differ from the broad plan in each direction. This option adds programming, algorithms, databases, machine learning, deep learning and image analysis. It gives more weight to quantitative and computational methods than to anatomy, epidemiology and health psychology.

alternatives.label: Human physiology, disease and mental health
alternatives.labelReason: The biomedical core spans physiology, infection, disease and pharmacology. Developmental psychology, psychological assessment and psychotherapy give this option a distinct emphasis on mental health and illustrate diagnosis and intervention in that domain.
alternatives.concept: Study human physiology, infection, disease and drug action alongside brain function and development. Examine psychological assessment and therapies to understand one way research informs diagnosis and treatment.
progression: The life-science and brain gateways precede dependent biomedical and behavioural courses. Laboratory and cell biology precede pathology and disease. Psychopathology precedes psychological assessment and therapies.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses differ from the broad plan in each direction. This option develops mental health and lifespan development through psychopathology, psychological assessment and therapies, and developmental psychology. Philosophy adds a complementary perspective on agency. The broad plan gives more weight to data, probability and evolution.

trace: Introduces cellular, genetic, physiological and disease-oriented biomedical reasoning.
Introduces nervous-system and behavioural foundations relevant to human health.
Connects epidemiology, prevention and population health with societal impact.
Develops molecular and cellular mechanisms central to biomedical science.
Develops experimental practice through aseptic culture, bacterial identification, protein work, PCR and interpretation of DNA results.
Supplies quantitative foundations for biomedical methods and modelling.
Covers integrated human physiology and organ-system function.
Builds biochemical understanding of metabolism and molecular function.
Connects inheritance, variation and genetic testing to pathology, including neoplasia and haematological disease.
Develops statistics, study design and experimental inference.
Provides functional human anatomy for organism and organ-system study.
Examines pathogens, immunity and infectious disease.
Integrates cellular and physiological mechanisms across major diseases.
Provides an ethical framework for health and research decisions.
Studies therapeutic mechanisms and pharmacological intervention.
Extends human neural and cognitive function at advanced level.
Connects health, behaviour, care and patient context.
Introduces reproducible data handling and quantitative analysis.
Examines neural mechanisms of perception and action through cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.
Develops systematic-review methods including searching, data extraction, bias appraisal and analysis of effects.
Develops probability and statistical modelling for biomedical evidence.
Provides programming foundations for bioinformatics and biomedical data.
Applies computational image analysis to complex visual data.
Builds and evaluates neural networks for prediction and image analysis. The methods can transfer to biomedical datasets.
Provides structured data management for large research datasets.
Applies machine learning to prediction and classification.
Examines psychopathology, classification and mechanisms of mental illness.
Examines philosophical accounts of agency and responsibility, which complement ethical reflection on mental health.
Examines diagnosis and evidence-based psychological treatment.
Tracks human development and health across the lifespan.
Examines genetic variation, inheritance and selection across populations, providing an evolutionary perspective on biological mechanisms.
Develops algorithm design, graph traversal and complexity analysis as transferable tools for computational research.
blocks: Both establish cellular and molecular foundations for human biomedical study.
Both study biomolecules, enzyme activity and metabolism.
Both study inheritance, variation and genetic information. UCR emphasises genetic testing and disease mechanisms.
UCR studies neoplasia and cancer mechanisms in pathology. Utrecht brings those questions together in a dedicated project on tumours and metastases.
Both integrate human physiology at organism and organ-system level.
UCR develops anatomy and structure–function reasoning. Utrecht studies differentiation and tissue types in greater depth.
Both study cellular signalling, membranes, gene regulation and cellular responses.
UCR studies population evidence and health interventions. Utrecht gives dedicated attention to collaboration among scientists, policymakers and the public.
UCR laboratory work supplies hands-on experimental practice within the comparator's broader compulsory methods component.
Utrecht requires supervised experimental work and a thesis. UCR teaches laboratory and evidence-review methods and offers optional independent research separately.
Both develop data analysis. Utrecht applies it to biological information, while UCR teaches general data handling and visualisation.
Students select a first-year biomedical elective from the official list.
Students complete at least four other courses from the restricted list in addition to Molecular Cell Biology.
The 45-EC profiling space remains open and is not treated as fixed comparator content.

selection.assessment: The broad option covers human biomedical mechanisms, laboratory methods and population health. The molecular option develops computational research methods. The physiology option develops mental health assessment, intervention and development within a biomedical composition. Each plan meets the minimum distinctness requirement.

notes.text: Utrecht requires an integrated biomedical major and a supervised research project with an English thesis. UCR offers molecular and human biology, laboratory methods, and quantitative and behavioural study. The UCR options provide preparation in these areas, while Utrecht requires dedicated bioinformatics and project-based research.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht Biomedical Sciences studies the human body in health and disease. The programme builds from cells, molecules, tissues and organ systems to laboratory and data methods. Students choose biomedical electives and complete a supervised research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The three UCR options emphasise broad biomedical science, molecular genetics and computational methods, or human physiology and mental health. They share laboratory and disease-focused study. Utrecht requires a dedicated bioinformatics course and an experimental project with a thesis.

curriculum.limitation: This outline shows the standard 15 EC research project and preserves the official biomedical electives and 45 EC of profiling space.

componentNotes.bmw-y1-choice: Choose from the first-year biomedical electives, which include ethics, evolutionary biology, introductory neuroscience and medical imaging.
componentNotes.bmw-major-choice: Complete at least five courses from the ten-course major list, including Moleculaire Biologie van de Cel. Major and degree-level requirements apply.
componentNotes.bmw-research: The standard 15 EC project combines a literature study, experimental work, an English thesis and a research-integrity module. Entry requires 150 EC. A 22.5 EC Plus option is available under separate rules.
componentNotes.bmw-profiling: At least 15 of these 45 EC must be at level 2 or 3. Course-entry and overlap rules apply.
